subject: Uptime safeguard retainer — structure, tiers & concession ask
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@silverfin.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime safeguard retainer — structure, tiers & concession ask

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. Per our conversation you wanted a compact retainer option that guarantees higher uptime handling for Silverfin's ingestion spikes and a clear escalation path for on-call routing. I attached a draft schedule (retainer_schedule_v2.pdf) and a short credit matrix.

High-level proposal:
- Uptime safeguard retainer (monthly): provides a dedicated response lane, 4-hour critical response SLO, and a pool of 24/7 escalation hours.
- Three tiers: Core (99.5%), Elevated (99.9%), Mission (99.95%) — each with escalating retention and QA-run playbooks.
- Discounts: 5% at 6-month commit, 10% at 12-month commit; additional concession possible tied to committed GPU-hours.

Questions for you:
1) Do you need the Mission tier across all regions or only us/eu?
2) Is a time-and-materials overage model acceptable if you exceed the escalation hours in a month?
3) Any procurement constraints around retainer invoicing frequency (monthly vs. quarterly)?

If you’re happy with this direction I can loop in Karthik for pricing flexibility and Soojin for contract clauses.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: retainer_schedule_v2.pdf)
From: Elena Park <elena@silverfin.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uptime safeguard retainer — structure, tiers & concession ask

Laura —

Thanks for the detailed proposal. Quick clarifications before we move to internal budgeting:
- We primarily need Elevated (99.9%) for ingestion pipelines in us and eu; Mission only for a small subset (payment validation) — can that be scoped to a subset of services?
- For overages: we prefer capped monthly overage vs open T&M. Would you consider a soft cap with 50% discount on overage hours past the retainer?
- Invoicing cadence: finance prefers quarterly invoices for retainer fees.

Also, can you provide an example incident playback and how credits would be applied? If you could forward the SLA credit matrix that’d help.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Ops, Silverfin Analytics
From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Uptime safeguard retainer — concession ask from Silverfin

Looping you in — Elena from Silverfin (prospect) asked for: 1) scoped Mission tier, 2) capped overages with a discount, 3) quarterly invoicing.

Karthik: can we offer a conditional concession — 8% discount at 12-month commit + capped overage at 150% of retainer hours billed at 50% discount? We should keep a hard cap to limit exposure.
Soojin: any procurement redlines we should anticipate for quarterly billing vs monthly?
Connor: can CS provide a short incident playback example and an annotated credit application to share?

Short timeline: Elena wants a revised commercial by EOD tomorrow to get through budget review next week.

- Laura
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime safeguard retainer — concession ask from Silverfin

Thanks Laura — quick take:
- Approve 8% discount at 12-month commit (we should preserve margin by tying to GPU-hour minimum).
- Approve capped overage at 150% of monthly retainer hours billed at 50% of list overage rate — add clause: discretionary relief for sustained incidents (>=3 days) to protect customer goodwill.
- Quarterly invoicing: OK but include a one-month upfront at kickoff and net-30 after each quarter to keep cashflow neutral.

Soojin: please review suggested wording: "Overage hours beyond the monthly retainer will be billed at 50% of the published T&M rate up to 150% of retainer hours; hours beyond that are billed at standard T&M. In sustained incident scenarios, Redwood may apply discretionary credits per the SLA credit matrix."

Connor: can you produce a short incident playback and attach the SLA_credit_matrix.xlsx? Laura will send to Elena.

-Karthik
From: Elena Park <elena@silverfin.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@silverfin.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uptime safeguard retainer — structure, tiers & concession ask

Laura —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the updated terms. We reviewed internally and can proceed with the following: 
- Elevated (99.9%) for all ingestion services in us + eu; Mission tier for the payment validation service only.
- We accept the 8% discount on a 12-month commitment and the capped overage structure as proposed (150% cap billed at 50% discounted rate) provided the discretionary credit language is included.
- Quarterly invoicing is fine; finance requests the first quarterly invoice after a one-month kickoff pro-rata.

Please send a revised commercial and contract addendum with the specific service scoping and the incident playback example. Once received, we'll route to procurement.

Regards,
Elena
Head of Platform Ops, Silverfin Analytics
(References: see attached SLA_credit_matrix.xlsx)
